h: Levanon Whitens Sin: Exile, Lavan's Daughters, and a Thousandfold Blessing
The Haftarah and Yaakov's Going into Exile

h: Levanon Three Times in the Haftarah

p: וְלָכֵן מַפְטִירִין בְּפָרָשַׁת שׁוּבָה יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹמֵר
— Therefore we read as the haftarah the passage "Return, O Israel" etc.,
— in which "Levanon" is mentioned three times.
— "I will be like the dew to Israel" (Hoshea 14:6) —
— that is, the "dew of Atika" the Ancient One,
— in which "And He said" is not stated,
— for it is the Hidden Intellect,
— "for the sake of Israel, who are called 'first' (reishit)."
— as is written in the holy Zohar
— "And he shall strike his roots like Levanon" —
— Because it whitens the sins of Israel."
— And it is written "and he shall strike his roots like Levanon,"
— for at the root they are bound and rooted.
— and this is along the lines of what they said
— will in the future give off fragrance."
— will in the future give off fragrance.
— And Rashi explained from Targum Yonatan:
— like the fragrance of the incense of spices."
— That is, into the incense they mixed galbanum,
— which alludes to the transgressors of Israel,
— among the spices of the incense."
— with the ten other spices of the incense.
— So too the transgressors of Israel will give off fragrance
— when they are bound together as one.
— "his remembrance like the wine of Levanon" (Hoshea 14:8);
(פְּסָחִים קו עַמּוּד א, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל זוֹכְרֵהוּ)
— and they also bring the verse
— "We will remember Your love more than wine" (Shir HaShirim 1:4)
— regarding the sanctification of the day (Kiddush).
— which is the wine of libations
— that is poured out in the Holy Temple,
— as is stated in Targum Yonatan.
— a place that has no forgetting,
— and in which no forgetting abides

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Korach 11:2: “And this is the matter of the incense, of which the holy Zohar says that the incense rises only by his hand, for he increases peace in the world. It too serves to repair Israel so that they stand in the state of ‘And your people are all righteous,’ for mixed into the incense was the galbanum as well, which points to the transgressors of Israel, as they learned from it (Keritot 6b): ‘Any fast that does not include some of the transgressors of Israel,’ and so on. That is, chelbenah (galbanum) is the letters of levanah, ‘white,’ with a chet added; and ‘white’ alludes to His future whitening of Israel's sins, as it is expounded (Yoma 39b), ‘Why is it called Levanon? Because it whitens the sins of Israel,’ and likewise (Bereishit Rabbah 70), ‘Do you know Lavan son of Nachor? Do you know the One who will in the future whiten your sins like snow?’ The added chet, which points to darkness, is the aspect of ‘He made darkness His hiding place,’ for He is hidden from all thought; through this the deeds of the wicked, the galbanum, branched off, since the light was hidden, and therefore the galbanum has a foul smell. But in truth the chet points to ‘He lives (chai) at the height of the world.’ For already in the utterance ‘Bereishit’ the deeds of the wicked are mentioned, which Hashem will refine: ‘If your sins be like these years that have been ordered and continuing since the six days of Creation, they shall become white as snow’ (Shabbat 89b). So it was in the beginning of Thought: first darkness and then light, for there is no light except that which comes out of darkness; and then even the galbanum will give off a good fragrance.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharsha, Chiddushei Aggados, Keritot 6b: “‘For galbanum has a foul smell, yet Scripture counted it,’ and so on: that is, the transgressor does not separate himself from the community. This is why he was careful to say ‘Scripture counted it’ and did not say ‘and one burns it with them’: he means that the transgressor is counted with them in their fast and does not separate from them. From this allusion one may learn that there were eleven kinds of incense, ten with a good fragrance and one, the galbanum, with a foul fragrance: the transgressor too is to be joined, but only when there is a holy congregation that makes up a quorum of ten without him; he is not to be joined as one of the ten. A reminder of this is ‘I will not destroy for the sake of the ten,’ while for fewer than ten Avraham did not pray. And Abaye, who said, ‘From here: and His bundle (agudato) He founded upon the earth,’ means the same: ‘His bundle’ is the ten holinesses, each one above the other, as the Midrashim say, and He ‘founded it upon the earth,’ the lowly one, which is counted together with them in Israel.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Nissim of Gerona, Derashot HaRan 1:4: “From this side, which nature itself has confirmed for us, our Sages, of blessed memory, spoke so greatly of the praise and the awe of the community, until they said, ‘Let the awe of the community always be upon you.’ ... They meant that although each one in himself is not worthy of this, by joining with others the whole acquires praise and stature beyond what its parts deserve, just as compounds acquire properties and virtues that were not in the separate things from which they were gathered. And they already hinted this to us in the galbanum that was placed among the spices of the incense: it would seem that it would spoil them with its foul smell, and yet prophecy confirmed for us that they have no completeness without it. So it is when the sinners and transgressors join with us in our service of Hashem, may He be blessed: they do not spoil our service; rather, it becomes more complete through them.”

h: Levanon in the Zohar: Binah and Da'at

p: — And in the holy Zohar on this parashah
— (162b, at the end of the page):
— That is, we find in the holy Zohar
— "for there is no voice without speech
— 'With me from Levanon, O bride' (Shir HaShirim 4:8),
— for the root of both of them
— That is, there it explains Levanon
— who gives birth to a son and a daughter,
— But here it explains Levanon as Da'at,
— which is the inwardness of Keter,
— This is like the Gemara's exposition:
— And this is "if your sins be like the years" —
— these years that have been ordered
— since the six days of Creation —
— And this is why it says "it has already been established":
— for the expositions of our Sages, of blessed memory,
— in the books of the revealed Torah,
— whereas for what is mentioned in the Sitrei Torah
— the expression is "we have already established,"
— And this is what it says:
— And these are the two birds
— of which we have spoken in several places, etc.,
— supernal ones, that issue forth from Levanon,
— and the secret of the matter is:
— that is Da'at, the inwardness of Keter;
— and this is why it says "which is above."
— And then they were in exile
— under the hand of Lavan, in the kelipah;
— and this is why it says "and the secret of the matter is:
— And this is the entire subject of the parashah.

h: One Unbroken Parashah: Bringing Out Knesset Yisrael

p: — there is no section break at all in it,
— to reflect between one section and the next,
— as stated at the beginning of Torat Kohanim,
— alluding to the building of Knesset Yisrael.
— And this is what it says in the holy Zohar
— "'If you are wise, you are wise for yourself' etc. (Mishlei 9:12):
— for all the words of the Torah,
— all of them are supernal and precious words,
— and of each and every word
— 'It is more precious than pearls' (Mishlei 3:15)," etc.;
— This is mentioned in several places,
— and it is written in this parashah specifically
— because it appears to be mere narratives,
— but in truth they are supernal secrets.
— The whole parashah is one undertaking:
— and brought out from under Lavan's hand
— in which Israel are bound at the root,
— "Our will is to do Your will" etc. (Berachot 17a);
— after the seven days of the wedding feast,
— to be refined seven times seven.
— to rectify the deeds and actions
— as it is written, "And your people are all righteous" (Yeshayahu 60:21),
— And this is the whole undertaking:
— that he brought out from under Lavan's hand
— And it is written, "The stork, the cypresses are her house" (Tehillim 104:17):
— the six sides of the world,
— as is written in the holy Zohar.
— for it gives birth to the six middot
— to bring out all of Knesset Yisrael.
— This is alluded to in what is stated
— that he had six hundred thousand flocks;
— and the number six hundred thousand
— to the souls of the Children of Israel,
— for the root of Knesset Yisrael
— and parts of letters in the Torah.
— And all his occupation then was:
— that he sifted out Knesset Yisrael,
— as is written in the holy Zohar
— "'And he did not put them with Lavan's flock':
— that he did not set his portion
— and his lot with them," etc.;
— (162a, at the end of the page):
— And this is the entire subject of the parashah:
— and Yaakov brought them out from there.
— And from this comes the theme of the haftarah,
— So too the Psalm of Shabbat
— begins "It is good to give thanks to Hashem" (Tehillim 92:2);
— that whoever confesses and forsakes his sins, etc.,
— as it is written, "He who confesses and forsakes shall obtain mercy" (Mishlei 28:13).
— And it concludes, "The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree;
, — he shall grow like a cedar in Levanon" (Tehillim 92:13).
— for Shabbat is a time of teshuvah,
— "If your sins be like the years" —
— these that have been ordered and continuing
— since the six days of Creation —

He said to them: This one is my own, but He will bless you as He has spoken to you” (from the Sifrei). The Midrash: “The Holy One, blessed be He, set no limit to our blessings, and you said ‘a thousand times’! He said to them: What I blessed you with, I blessed you from my own.” The Midrash also explains that God's "addition" is greater than the principal.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 161a (Vayetzei): “R. Abba said: A thousand sheep, a thousand lambs and a thousand goats Yaakov would bring him in addition, each and every month ... and blessing from above is not less than a thousand of each and every kind.” Yaakov brought Lavan an extra thousand of each every month, for blessing from above is never less than a thousand of each kind. The Zohar reads "hava maytei" and "lav" where the print has "havu" and "la."

h: Shabbat's Blessing and the Days Around It

p: — as it is written, "And God blessed
— the blessing of Hashem is without measure;
— for the six days of work is measured.
— As the Ari, of blessed memory, reckoned:
— that in the three days after Shabbat
— in the levels of Neshamah, Ruach, Nefesh;
— and in the three days before Shabbat
— there is the shining forth of holiness
— in the levels of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah.
— correspond to the three worlds mentioned,
— as is written in Tikkunei Zohar
— and from the Ofan the nefashot;
— and they are in Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah," etc.
— is from the World of Asiyah,
— And when the impression of holiness remains
— for the three days after Shabbat,
— of Hashem, may He be blessed,
— in the three days before Shabbat,
— a thousand from the holiness of the coming Shabbat,
— as He has spoken to you" —
— for the blessing of Hashem, may He be blessed,
— "And Hashem has blessed you on my account."
— The blessing of Hashem is without measure,
— Lavan did not merit at all,
— upon Lavan by Yaakov our father, peace be upon him.
— And this is what the holy Zohar counted:
— "a thousand sheep, a thousand lambs," etc.,
— that Yaakov our father bestowed upon Lavan;
— and he said that the addition from the blessing
— from Hashem, may He be blessed,
— was merited by Yaakov our father, peace be upon him.
— who are the root of holiness,

paragraphs.text: Sha'ar HaKavanot, Sermons on the Order of the Sabbath 1:4: “All three remain with a person on the first day of the week; on the night of the second day the Neshamah departs and the Nefesh and Ruach remain; on the night of the third day the Ruach departs; and on the night of the fourth day the Nefesh also departs. After that one must make a new rectification and receive the addition of all three on the three remaining days.” The added Neshamah, Ruach and Nefesh all stay through Sunday; on the night that begins Monday the Neshamah leaves, on the night that begins Tuesday the Ruach, and on the night that begins Wednesday the Nefesh. On the three days left one must receive all three again for the coming Shabbat.  This is the source of Rav Tzadok's order: Neshamah-Ruach-Nefesh after Shabbat, Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah before it.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sidduro Shel Shabbat, Volume II, Derush II 2:18 (Chassidus): cites the same teaching of the Ari: the three days before Shabbat belong to it as preparation, and Shabbat then shines into the three days after it. He describes Shabbat as standing in the middle, both receiving and giving, while Rav Tzadok counts the flow by worlds.

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar 23a (Tikkun 6): “And so Metatron pleads in defense of his birds, which are the spirits that fly among human beings. From the Throne come the neshamot, from this Chayah the ruchot, and from the Ofan the nefashot; and they are in Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah.” This is part of Tikkun 6, on the mitzvah of sending away the mother bird.
